sources.matrix: own transitions (0.0, weighted by the HMM's regime probabilities) + the panel's HMM matrix (695 companies, 9156 company-years) at K = 6
sources.regimes: hidden Markov model of yearly growth, pooled over 695 companies (9156 company-years, annual XBRL frames since 2010): regimes average +30.7%, +9.8%, +5.1%
sources.now: the HMM's probability of each regime in the latest year: 8% / 30% / 61%
sources.growth: the HMM's regime means and spreads (1645/3646/3866 company-years per regime); spreads × 1.5, fitted in the walk-forward backtest so that the 80% range of revenue three years out holds about 80% of what happened (as estimated, the spreads made it too narrow)

backtest.text: Backtest (run in 2013–2019 on every filer's data as of then, 2,274 outcomes, without analysts' consensus): the 80% range of revenue three years out held 80% of what happened (11% fell below it, 9% above) — about right. That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.
